Olga / Laura — I reviewed the questionnaire and sketched answers in the attached draft (Redwood_Draft_Termset_Answers_v1.docx). High-level position proposals:

1) IP / Outputs: we will not assign ownership of the base model weights or any open models; for customer-provided prompts/data and derivative outputs, we propose a license to the customer to use, reproduce, and sublicense outputs for their internal and customer-facing uses. We can include an optional addendum for explicit assignment for regulated customers on a case-by-case basis.

2) Indemnity: we can accept a limited IP infringement indemnity for claims arising from our implementation (i.e., model outputs that directly reproduce a third-party work), but we need carve-outs:
   - No indemnity for claims arising solely from customer-provided content or customer instructions that resulted in the output.
   - No indemnity for uses outside the scope of the contract (e.g., model fine-tuning with customer data without separate agreement).

3) Liability cap: propose a 24-month rolling cap based on actual fees paid in the prior 12 months (or 24 months if preferred), with carve-outs for willful misconduct and breach of confidentiality. This balances customer protection and provider risk.

Laura — legal to confirm wording and cross-check against our standard Exhibits (IP Exhibit / Order Form).

Karthik

Team — attached updated answers with legal phrasing. Key edits I made:
- IP outputs: replaced 'assignment' language with a permanent, royalty-free, worldwide license to the customer for outputs, with an optional SOW for assignment where required.
- Indemnity: narrowed Redwood indemnity to third-party IP claims alleging the service infringes their IP; included explicit exceptions for customer data/inputs and for open-source model components that we clearly attribute.
- Liability cap: standardized to 'aggregate damages shall not exceed the greater of (i) fees paid in the prior 12 months or (ii) $250,000' but added asks: we should offer commercial flexibility to move to 24-months or higher cap for enterprise reserved deals.

Also added an Order Form summary that maps how subscription fees are calculated (tokens, reserved capacity, overage rates) for their finance team. See Redwood_SLA_and_OrderForm_Summary.pdf attached.

Please review and sign off so I can send back to MediSys legal.

Laura

Laura / Olga — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear answers. A few points from our counsel (Alan) below. Overall: good progress but we still have two negotiation points.

Alan's notes (summarized):
- Outputs: they will accept a license but ask for a limited right to sublicense for integration partners; can you confirm sublicensing is allowed for customer-provided outputs used to deliver services to MediSys customers?
- Indemnity: they pushed back on carve-out language for customer inputs — they would like Redwood to cover infringement claims even where customer content is involved unless the customer had actual knowledge of infringement. Could you confirm Redwood's position on this?
- Liability cap: they prefer a 12-month fees cap but open to 24-months with tiered pricing. Would Redwood consider a middle ground: 18-month cap for enterprise customers with reserved capacity?

Can you provide a brief response to these three bullets (sublicense, customer-input carve-out, 18-month cap) by EOD Tuesday 10/14 so we can move to final redline?

Thanks,
Grace

Subject: Re: MediSys RFP – Terms questionnaire: IP, indemnity & liability cap (short answers)

Grace / Alan — appreciate the detailed feedback. Short answers below; Laura included finalized language in the attached drive link for your counsel to redline.

1) Sublicensing for outputs: Yes — Redwood will permit the customer to sublicense outputs to integration partners for the purpose of delivering services to MediSys customers, provided (a) sublicenses are limited to use of those outputs, (b) customer remains liable for sublicensee misuse, and (c) we have the right to audit compliance in a narrow way.

2) Indemnity for customer inputs: Redwood cannot provide a blanket indemnity where the customer knowingly provided infringing material. We are willing to accept indemnity unless there is evidence of customer knowledge or willful blindness. Proposed clause: Redwood indemnifies for third-party IP claims arising from the service, except where the claim results solely from (i) customer-provided content that the customer knew was infringing, or (ii) modifications made by the customer outside of the service scope.

3) Liability cap: We can agree to a middle-ground 18-month cap on fees for enterprise reserved capacity deals (Reserved/Dedicated with annual commitment). For hosted/standard contracts, we prefer the 12-month fees cap or the $250,000 floor.

Next steps: Laura will send the formal redline to Alan; Olga will follow up with procurement on whether MediSys wants the Reserved capacity commercial path.

Best,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
